name: Hanok Village (Pungnam-dong)
tagline: Living heritage of traditional tiled roofs
description: The postcard heart of Jeonju, a large district of several hundred traditional hanok houses alongside the Gyeonggijeon Shrine and Jeondong Catholic Church. Cobbled lanes, craft workshops, tea houses and street food make it atmospheric but busy with visitors.
bestFor: culture lovers and short-stay visitors wanting heritage on their doorstep

name: Gaeksa Downtown
tagline: Central shopping and everyday city buzz
description: Jeonju's main downtown around the historic Gaeksa, packed with shops, chain and independent cafes, restaurants and street life. It is the practical hub for daily errands and casual working, walkable from the Hanok Village and lively into the evening.
bestFor: nomads wanting shops, cafes and central convenience for daily life
pros: Plenty of cafes to work from

name: Jeonbuk University Area
description: The lively quarter around Jeonbuk National University, full of cheap eateries, study cafes, bars and budget rentals. Its student population gives it a young, affordable feel, with quiet zones for focused work and a sociable evening scene near campus.
bestFor: budget-minded remote workers who like a youthful, energetic setting
pros: Study cafes with power and wifi

name: Deokjin Park (Deokjin-dong)
tagline: Green, calm and residential lakeside living
description: A leafier residential area centred on Deokjin Park, known for its lotus pond and walking paths. Quieter and more local than the tourist core, it suits those wanting greenery, calm streets and a settled everyday rhythm within reach of the city.
bestFor: longer-stay nomads wanting calm, greenery and a local everyday pace
